name: OOP & C++
blurb: Full-length talks and lectures, chosen for mastery: how C++ objects, ownership, templates and concurrency really work, from people who write the compilers, libraries and the standard. Expect about an hour per best pick.
method:
• Best pick: the most thorough correct treatment of the subtopic, usually a 50–70 minute CppCon talk. Length was not held against a video; ten-minute summaries could not be best picks.
  • Then watch: the talk that completes the subject, such as part two or the mechanism underneath.
  • Go deeper: expert material past the usual interview line: standard-library implementers, compiler engineers and language designers.
  • Quick / visual: short refreshers for after you know the material, never a substitute for it.
  • Candidates came from YouTube links in Hacker News comments plus YouTube search for every subtopic. Popular beginner tutorials and one-shot crash courses lost to talks that show the mechanism. Picks were chosen from speaker, topic, length and recommendations; they were not all watched end to end.

subtopics.name: Full courses
subtopics.note: Pick one structured course for the language, then use the subtopics below for depth. The CppCon track is the spine of this page.

picks.title: Modern C++ (Lecture & Tutorials, 2020, Vizzo & Stachniss)
picks.why: University of Bonn's Modern C++ course with lectures and tutorials: build systems, memory, classes, templates, the STL and tooling. The most complete university-style C++ course here.

picks.title: The C++ Programming Language
picks.why: Mike Shah's long-running series, one concept per episode, through modern features and how they behave. Use it as a reference when a single topic needs another explanation.

picks.title: CppCon 2021 - Back To Basics
picks.why: CppCon's 2021 Back to Basics track. The name undersells it: each talk is an hour on one core feature, given by a practising expert.

picks.title: C++
picks.why: The Cherno's short episodes. Good for a first look or a fast refresher, not enough on their own for mastery.

subtopics.name: OOP Foundations
subtopics.note: Encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and abstraction, then the harder question: when is a class hierarchy the wrong tool, and what do you pay for it?

picks.title: Back to Basics: Object-Oriented Programming - Jon Kalb - CppCon 2019
picks.why: Inheritance, virtual functions, overriding and the rules that trip people up in C++, taught from the language's actual semantics instead of animal analogies.

picks.title: Back to Basics: Designing Classes (part 1 of 2) - Klaus Iglberger - CppCon 2021
picks.why: How to design a class that stays correct: invariants, ownership of resources, what belongs inside and what doesn't. Part one of two.

picks.title: Back to Basics: Designing Classes (part 2 of 2) - Klaus Iglberger - CppCon 2021
picks.why: Part two: the design of interfaces, data members and class hierarchies.

picks.title: Bjarne Stroustrup - The Essence of C++
picks.why: Bjarne Stroustrup on what C++ is for: resource management, abstraction without overhead, and where object orientation fits among the styles it supports.

picks.title: Better Code: Runtime Polymorphism - Sean Parent
picks.why: Sean Parent's case that inheritance should be an implementation detail, building runtime polymorphism on value types. The talk that changes how you see the first three.

picks.title: Casey Muratori – The Big OOPs: Anatomy of a Thirty-five-year Mistake – BSC 2025
picks.why: Casey Muratori's historical critique of compile-time class hierarchies. Long and opinionated. Useful for answering "what are the downsides of OOP?" from evidence.

subtopics.name: Virtual Dispatch & Object Layout
subtopics.note: What a vtable and vptr actually are, object layout under single and multiple inheritance, how dynamic_cast finds its answer, and what a virtual call costs.

picks.title: C++ Under the Hood: Internal Class Mechanisms - Chris Ryan - CppCon 2024
picks.why: Walks through how classes are laid out and how internal class mechanisms such as virtual calls work underneath.

picks.title: CppCon 2017: Arthur O'Dwyer “dynamic_cast From Scratch”
picks.why: Rebuilds dynamic_cast by hand, which forces you through RTTI, vtable contents and base-class offsets.

picks.title: Using Modern C++ to Eliminate Virtual Functions - Jonathan Gopel - CppCon 2022
picks.why: Compile-time alternatives to virtual functions and what they trade away. Know these before claiming virtual calls should be avoided.

subtopics.name: Object Lifetime, RAII & Special Members
subtopics.note: When the compiler generates each special member, the rules of zero, three and five, construction and destruction order, and copy elision.

picks.title: Back To Basics: The Special Member Functions - Klaus Iglberger - CppCon 2021
picks.why: All six special member functions: when each is generated, suppressed or deleted, and how to write them correctly.

picks.title: Back to Basics: RAII and the Rule of Zero - Arthur O'Dwyer - CppCon 2019
picks.why: RAII from first principles, why the rule of three exists, and how the rule of zero removes the problem.

picks.title: CppCon 2018: Jason Turner “Surprises in Object Lifetime”
picks.why: Lifetime extension, temporaries and dangling references, through examples that look correct and are not.

picks.title: C++ RVO: Return Value Optimization for Performance in Bloomberg C++ Codebases - Michelle Fae D'Souza
picks.why: Return value optimization in a large production codebase: when it applies and which code silently loses it.

picks.title: Return Value Optimization and Copy Elision in C++
picks.why: A ten-minute refresher on RVO and copy elision.

subtopics.name: Move Semantics & Value Categories
subtopics.note: lvalues, xvalues and prvalues; rvalue references; what a moved-from object may do; and how std::move and std::forward differ. Interviewers probe this one hard.

picks.title: Back to Basics: Move Semantics (part 1 of 2) -  Klaus Iglberger - CppCon 2019
picks.why: The careful treatment of rvalue references and how to write move operations. Part one of two.

picks.title: Back to Basics: Move Semantics (part 2 of 2) - Klaus Iglberger - CppCon 2019
picks.why: Part two: perfect forwarding, forwarding references and the conditions under which moves are generated.

picks.title: Back to Basics: Understanding Value Categories - Ben Saks - CppCon 2019
picks.why: Value categories explained properly, which makes the rules in the move talks follow from something.

picks.title: CppCon 2017: Nicolai Josuttis “The Nightmare of Move Semantics for Trivial Classes”
picks.why: Standard-committee member Nicolai Josuttis on how moves go wrong even for simple classes.

picks.title: Moved-from Objects in C++ - Jon Kalb - CppCon 2024
picks.why: What state a moved-from object is in, and what your types should promise about it.

picks.title: Move Semantics in C++
picks.why: A thirteen-minute introduction. Watch it first if rvalue references are new.

subtopics.name: Type Deduction
subtopics.note: The template, auto and decltype deduction rules. Most surprising C++ behaviour around references and const comes from here.

picks.title: CppCon 2014: Scott Meyers "Type Deduction and Why You Care"
picks.why: Scott Meyers lays out the deduction rules for templates, auto, lambda captures and decltype, and why each differs.

picks.title: CppCon 2014: Herb Sutter "Back to the Basics! Essentials of Modern C++ Style"
picks.why: Herb Sutter's guidance on auto, smart pointers and parameter passing in modern C++, including when the common advice is wrong.

picks.title: C++ Weekly - Ep 344 - decltype(auto): An Overview of How, Why and Where
picks.why: A short overview of decltype(auto) for revision.

subtopics.name: Smart Pointers & Ownership
subtopics.note: unique_ptr, shared_ptr and weak_ptr semantics, the control block and its atomic reference count, and how to express ownership in an interface.

picks.title: CppCon 2019: Arthur O'Dwyer “Back to Basics: Smart Pointers”
picks.why: Arthur O'Dwyer on how the standard smart pointers behave and how they are built.

picks.title: Back to Basics: C++ Smart Pointers - David Olsen - CppCon 2022
picks.why: A second full treatment focused on using each pointer type correctly and choosing between them.

picks.title: CppCon 2016: Herb Sutter “Leak-Freedom in C++... By Default.”
picks.why: Herb Sutter works up from simple ownership to cycles and graph structures, showing how far smart pointers can go without leaks.

picks.title: SMART POINTERS in C++ (std::unique_ptr, std::shared_ptr, std::weak_ptr)
picks.why: A twelve-minute introduction to the three types.

subtopics.name: Templates, Concepts & Metaprogramming
subtopics.note: Instantiation, specialisation, SFINAE, concepts, variadics and type erasure: the machinery behind the standard library.

picks.title: Back to Basics: Templates in C++ - Nicolai Josuttis - CppCon 2022
picks.why: Function and class templates from Nicolai Josuttis, including the instantiation rules behind the error messages.

picks.title: Back to Basics: Concepts in C++ - Nicolai Josuttis - CppCon 2024
picks.why: Concepts: how constraints replace SFINAE and what they do to overload resolution.

picks.title: Back to Basics: Type Erasure - Arthur O'Dwyer - CppCon 2019
picks.why: Type erasure built up from scratch, the technique behind std::function and std::any.

picks.title: CppCon 2014: Walter E. Brown "Modern Template Metaprogramming: A Compendium, Part I"
picks.why: Walter Brown's compendium of metaprogramming technique. Part one of the standard reference talk.

picks.title: CppCon 2014: Walter E. Brown "Modern Template Metaprogramming: A Compendium, Part II"
picks.why: Part two: void_t and the detection idioms the standard library uses.

picks.title: C++ Weekly - Ep 194 - From SFINAE To Concepts With C++20
picks.why: Thirteen minutes comparing the same constraint written with SFINAE and with concepts.

subtopics.name: STL Containers, Iterators & Algorithms
subtopics.note: Iterator categories and invalidation, complexity guarantees, what each container costs in memory and cache misses, and the algorithms that replace hand-written loops.

picks.title: Back to Basics: Iterators in C++ - Nicolai Josuttis - CppCon 2023
picks.why: Iterators from Nicolai Josuttis: categories, validity rules and how to use them without undefined behaviour.

picks.title: CppCon 2018: Jonathan Boccara “105 STL Algorithms in Less Than an Hour”
picks.why: A structured map of the standard algorithms so you recognise which one a problem needs.

picks.title: CppCon 2017: Matt Kulukundis “Designing a Fast, Efficient, Cache-friendly Hash Table, Step by Step”
picks.why: Designing Google's flat hash table step by step. Covers why std::unordered_map is slow and how cache-friendly tables are built.

picks.title: CppCon 2016: Nicholas Ormrod “The strange details of std::string at Facebook"
picks.why: How std::string is implemented at Facebook, with small-string optimisation and the bugs from changing it.

picks.title: CppCon 2015: Sean Parent "Better Code: Data Structures"
picks.why: Sean Parent on data structures as a design decision and the relationships that containers encode.

picks.title: GoingNative 2013 C++ Seasoning
picks.why: The source of "no raw loops": rewriting real code around algorithms.

subtopics.name: Memory & Allocators
subtopics.note: Stack and heap, how new and malloc get memory, allocator interfaces, arenas and pools, and why allocation dominates so many profiles.

picks.title: CppCon 2017: Bob Steagall “How to Write a Custom Allocator”
picks.why: Writing a standard-conforming custom allocator, which requires understanding the whole allocator model.

picks.title: CppCon 2017: John Lakos “Local ('Arena') Memory Allocators (part 1 of 2)”
picks.why: John Lakos with measurements of when local arena allocators help and when they do not. Part one of two.

picks.title: CppCon 2015: Andrei Alexandrescu “std::allocator...”
picks.why: Andrei Alexandrescu critiques the std::allocator design and composes better allocators from small parts.

picks.title: Allocators, Explained Simply
picks.why: Ten minutes on what an allocator is, for orientation.

subtopics.name: Concurrency, Atomics & the Memory Model
subtopics.note: std::thread and mutexes, atomics, memory orders and happens-before, lock-free structures and what the hardware does beneath them.

picks.title: Back to Basics: Concurrency - Arthur O'Dwyer - CppCon 2020
picks.why: The C++ concurrency toolkit: threads, mutexes, condition variables, atomics and the mistakes each invites.

picks.title: CppCon 2017: Fedor Pikus “C++ atomics, from basic to advanced.  What do they really do?”
picks.why: Fedor Pikus on what atomics actually do, including cost and the meaning of the memory orders.

picks.title: C++ and Beyond 2012: Herb Sutter - atomic Weapons 1 of 2
picks.why: Herb Sutter's definitive memory-model lecture, part one: sequential consistency, acquire and release, and the transformations compilers and CPUs make.

picks.title: C++ and Beyond 2012: Herb Sutter - atomic Weapons 2 of 2
picks.why: Part two: the same model across x86, ARM and POWER, and what compilers emit.

picks.title: CppCon 2014: Herb Sutter "Lock-Free Programming (or, Juggling Razor Blades), Part I"
picks.why: Lock-free programming from Herb Sutter: reasoning about correctness when there is no lock. Part one of two.

picks.title: Single Producer Single Consumer Lock-free FIFO From the Ground Up - Charles Frasch - CppCon 2023
picks.why: Builds a single-producer single-consumer queue step by step, including its cache behaviour. A common low-latency exercise.

subtopics.name: Undefined Behaviour & the Compilation Model
subtopics.note: Translation units, the one-definition rule, linking and symbols, startup, and what undefined behaviour licenses an optimiser to do.

picks.title: Back to Basics: Compiling and Linking - Ben Saks - CppCon 2021
picks.why: What the compiler and linker each do, and how declarations, definitions and linkage produce the errors you see.

picks.title: CppCon 2016: Chandler Carruth “Garbage In, Garbage Out: Arguing about Undefined Behavior..."
picks.why: Chandler Carruth, an LLVM optimiser engineer, on what undefined behaviour means and why it exists.

picks.title: CppCon 2018: Matt Godbolt “The Bits Between the Bits: How We Get to main()”
picks.why: Matt Godbolt traces how a program gets to main(): the linker, global constructors and the loader.

picks.title: CppCon 2017: Matt Godbolt “What Has My Compiler Done for Me Lately? Unbolting the Compiler's Lid”
picks.why: Godbolt reads compiler output to show which optimisations you get for free and which abstractions cost nothing.

picks.title: How the C++ Linker Works
picks.why: Sixteen minutes on what the linker does, for orientation.

subtopics.name: Exceptions & Error Handling
subtopics.note: Stack unwinding, the basic, strong and nothrow guarantees, noexcept and how it affects moves, and the alternatives to exceptions.

picks.title: Back to Basics: Exceptions - Klaus Iglberger - CppCon 2020
picks.why: How exceptions behave and how to write code with correct exception guarantees.

picks.title: CppCon 2014: Jon Kalb "Exception-Safe Code, Part I"
picks.why: The start of Jon Kalb's three-part course on exception-safe code, the most thorough treatment of the guarantees.

picks.title: CppCon 2017: Dave Watson “C++ Exceptions and Stack Unwinding”
picks.why: What happens at runtime when an exception is thrown, down to unwind tables and where the cost goes.

picks.title: De-fragmenting C++: Making Exceptions and RTTI More Affordable and Usable - Herb Sutter  CppCon 2019
picks.why: Herb Sutter on why exceptions and RTTI are costly and how the language could change that.

picks.title: CppCon 2018: Andrei Alexandrescu “Expect the expected”
picks.why: Andrei Alexandrescu on expected-style error handling as an alternative to throwing.

subtopics.name: Design Principles & Patterns
subtopics.note: SOLID applied to real code, the classic patterns and what each one is for, and how value-based design replaces deep hierarchies.

picks.title: Breaking Dependencies: The SOLID Principles - Klaus Iglberger - CppCon 2020
picks.why: All five SOLID principles as tools for managing dependencies, in C++ with concrete refactorings.

picks.title: Design Patterns: Facts and Misconceptions - Klaus Iglberger - CppCon 2021
picks.why: What patterns are and are not, and the misconceptions about them that lead to poor answers.

picks.title: Breaking Dependencies - C++ Type Erasure - The Implementation Details - Klaus Iglberger  CppCon 2022
picks.why: Type erasure as a design pattern, with the implementation details that matter.

picks.title: Sean Parent: Value Semantics and Concepts-based Polymorphism
picks.why: Sean Parent's fuller lecture on value semantics and concept-based polymorphism.

picks.title: C++ Design Patterns - The Most Common Misconceptions (2 of N) - Klaus Iglberger - CppCon 2024
picks.why: More common misconceptions about specific patterns from Klaus Iglberger.

subtopics.name: Performance-Minded C++
subtopics.note: Data structures chosen for the memory hierarchy, benchmarking, and writing C++ with latency in mind.

picks.title: CppCon 2014: Chandler Carruth "Efficiency with Algorithms, Performance with Data Structures"
picks.why: Chandler Carruth on why cache behaviour usually matters more than the algorithm on paper, and how to choose data structures accordingly.

picks.title: CppCon 2014: Mike Acton "Data-Oriented Design and C++"
picks.why: Mike Acton's data-oriented design talk, the most-linked C++ video on Hacker News in this search (47 users). Argues that the data's shape should drive the code.

picks.title: CppCon 2019: Chandler Carruth “There Are No Zero-cost Abstractions”
picks.why: Shows measured costs of abstractions that are advertised as free.

picks.title: CppCon 2017: Carl Cook “When a Microsecond Is an Eternity: High Performance Trading Systems in C++”
picks.why: Techniques from low-latency trading systems: hot paths, branch handling, allocation and cache warming.

picks.title: When Nanoseconds Matter: Ultrafast Trading Systems in C++ - David Gross - CppCon 2024
picks.why: A more recent low-latency talk on queues, order books and measuring nanoseconds.

picks.title: Branchless Programming in C++ - Fedor Pikus - CppCon 2021
picks.why: Fedor Pikus on when removing branches pays off, with measurements.
